title: Azure Resource Manager
description: Discover how Azure Resource Manager (ARM) provides a consistent management layer, resource providers, and ARM templates.

data.text: Every request you send to Azure — whether through the Portal, CLI, PowerShell, or an SDK — goes through **Azure Resource Manager (ARM)**. ARM is the management layer that handles authentication, authorization, and the actual creation, update, or deletion of resources.

data.title: Benefits of ARM
items: **Consistent interface** — Use the same tools and APIs for every resource
**Role-based access control** — Manage who can do what at the resource group or subscription level
**Tagging and billing** — All resources support tags through ARM
**Resource locking** — Prevent accidental changes or deletions
**Template deployments** — Deploy entire environments as code with ARM templates

data.text: Each Azure service has a **resource provider** — the service that actually provides the resource. For example, Microsoft.Compute provides virtual machines, and Microsoft.Storage provides storage accounts. Every resource type follows the pattern `{resourceProvider}/{resourceType}`.

data.title: Common Resource Providers
data.code:
Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines
Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts
Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks
Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases
Microsoft.Web/sites
Microsoft.Insights/metricsAlerts

data.text: ARM exposes a REST API that all management tools use. Every operation — creating a VM, updating a tag, or deleting a database — is ultimately an HTTP request to the ARM API. The CLI and PowerShell are just friendlier wrappers around this API.

An **ARM template** is a JSON file that declares the infrastructure you want to deploy. Instead of clicking through the Portal, you write a template and let ARM create everything in one step. This is the foundation of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) on Azure.

terms.definition: The management layer that handles all Azure resource operations through a consistent API.
A service that provides one or more resource types, such as Microsoft.Compute for virtual machines.
The type of resource within a provider, such as virtualMachines under Microsoft.Compute.
A JSON file that declares Azure infrastructure as code for repeatable deployments.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ARM is the single management layer for all Azure resources
Resource providers define what services are available
ARM templates let you deploy infrastructure as code
The ARM REST API is what all Azure tools use behind the scenes
data.takeaway: Understanding ARM is key to mastering Azure, because everything you do in Azure flows through it.
